=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/render_prompt.py
  Line or code reference: lines ~757-759 (validate_supported_template_syntax function)
  Problem: The validation logic rejects ALL lines containing `{%` or `%}` as unsupported template syntax. This incorrectly rejects valid `{% include "..." %}` directives used by the Phase O template system. The check `if "{%" in line or "%}" in line:` is overly broad and breaks template includes.
  Why it fails at runtime: Running `scripts/render_prompt.sh prompts/mode-clarify-respond.txt` (or any newly-migrated mode) with `PROMPT_PRELUDE_REFACTOR_ENABLED=true` will abort with `ERROR: Unsupported template syntax: ... unsupported template tag syntax '{% include "_prelude_common.txt" %}'`, preventing prompt assembly for all Phase O templates.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 273-276
  Problem: The shell script unconditionally exits with code 0 when `ASSEMBLED_PROMPT_FILE` is set, regardless of the Python renderer's exit code. This masks any failures from the Python renderer, including validation failures.
  Why it fails at runtime: When the workflow sets `ASSEMBLED_PROMPT_FILE`, the shell runs the Python renderer but then ignores its exit status and always returns success (exit 0). This causes the pipeline to proceed even when prompt rendering fails, leading to downstream issues with empty or malformed prompts.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- Requirement: "Make the assembly/render path fail closed on unsupported template syntax, including filter-style expressions"
  Expected change site: scripts/render_prompt.py (validate_supported_template_syntax)
  Evidence of absence: The PR correctly rejects filter-style expressions (e.g., `{{FOO|lower}}`, `{{ .foo|default("x") }}`) and stray `}}` in prose, but does NOT add any regression test that exercises `{% include "..." %}` directives being accepted. Without a test confirming includes are allowed, a future edit could break include handling silently.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- File: scripts/render_prompt.py
  Line or code reference: 1007
  Problem: `validate_supported_template_syntax` is called unconditionally during the `--assemble-only` path, but the script does not ensure the Python process exits non-zero when a TemplateSyntaxError is raised, masking failure semantics in the shell wrapper.
  Why it fails at runtime: An uncaught `TemplateSyntaxError` prints an error to stderr and exits the Python process nonzero, but `scripts/render_prompt.sh`’s expectations for fail-closed behavior rely on a renderer exit code that scripts can test. Without catching and converting the exception to controlled stderr with stderr exit code set properly (currently it exits Python nonzero which the shell reads as failure, but with mixed diagnostic noise), CI can misattribute uncaught Python failures vs controlled validation rejections.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/render_prompt.py
  Line or code reference: 730-767
  Problem: `validate_supported_template_syntax` rejects `{% include "..." %}` directives as “unsupported template tag syntax”, incorrectly flagging valid shared-prelude includes used by all newly-migrated active modes.
  Why it fails at runtime: The shared-prelude system relies on `{% include "_prelude_*.txt" %}` directives, but the validator treats `{%` and `%}` as violations. Thus, running `scripts/render_prompt.sh mode-clarify-respond.txt` (and similar modes) under strict assembly will fail with `ERROR: unsupported template tag syntax '{% include "_prelude_common.txt" %}'`, contradicting the hard requirement to fail closed only on unsupported syntax.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- File: scripts/render_prompt.py
  Line or code reference: validate_supported_template_syntax(), lines ~754-759
  Problem: The template syntax validator unconditionally rejects any line containing `{%` or `%}` as unsupported template tag syntax, including valid `{% include "..." %}` directives that are the core mechanism of the shared-prelude template system.
  Why it fails at runtime: When `PROMPT_PRELUDE_REFACTOR_ENABLED=true`, the validator runs on assembled prompts. Although `collect_prompt_fragments()` processes include directives, any `{%` pattern remaining in the assembled output (e.g., from nested includes or metadata comments) triggers a validation error. The newly migrated templates at `prompts/_templates/mode-*.txt` all begin with `{% include "_prelude_common.txt" %}`; if assembly fails to completely resolve these or if any other template tag syntax appears in the output, assembled prompts fail validation with "unsupported template tag syntax", breaking the Phase O shared-prelude rollout.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
